content.text:
This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Breakers 52-M2 and CB-10 both trip at the same moment. Nothing else changes: no other breaker opens or closes, normally-open (N.O.) breakers stay open, and Standby generator G1 is not running and does not start. A load has power only if a path of closed breakers connects it to a running source. Which loads that were running before the event have no power afterwards? A load behind an open breaker was not running. Answer with the load tags (for example CH-2), in the order they appear on the drawing from left to right, separated by commas.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
52-M2 trips, de-energizing Bus 2. The normally-open tie to Bus 1 stays open, so Bus 1 remains powered but Bus 2 and Bus E lose their running source; G1 is unavailable. Bus 1B loses its Bus E feed through CB-9, and its CB-04 alternate feed is open. Bus 2B also has no alternate feed because CB-05 is open. CB-10’s trip additionally disconnects ELP-1. Loads on Bus 1 and Bus EB remain powered from Bus 1.

FINAL ANSWER: PP-2, CH-2, BP-1, HP-2, KP-1, LP-2, CT-1, ELP-1
